title: When the Mixtape Burns
premise: Vesper Oyelaran, seventeen and de facto parent to two younger siblings, has built a life on caution — until a group chat of five classmates begins receiving predictions that come true with unsettling precision. The messages trace back to the Founders' Game, a century-old town tradition on the verge of being cancelled, and each member of the chat is bound to it by an ancestor's bargain. As the predictions turn from harmless to dangerous, Vesper must choose between the safe, invisible life they've engineered for their family and stepping into the center of a mystery that demands risk. In the end, Vesper breaks the bargain by refusing to play the game as written — rewriting the tradition itself so no one has to pay the price of survival alone.
about_author: S. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a Nigerian-British writer who grew up between Lagos and a small rust-belt American town, a duality that shapes their stories about belonging. They write young adult fiction about kids who carry too much too early, and they still make mixtapes for people they love.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A night in the Oyelaran household: packing lunches, checking homework, covering for Mom's double shift at the hospital. Establishes Vesper's competence and exhaustion, and the quiet ache of a childhood traded away. Emotional beat: love expressed as vigilance, and the loneliness inside it.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Five classmates — Vesper, Theo, Priya, Marcus, and June — discover they've all been added to a group chat called LAST GAME that none of them created. The first message predicts tomorrow's weather down to the minute. It's right. Emotional beat: uneasy curiosity cracking through Vesper's instinct to ignore anything uncontrolled.

chapters.title: Small Prophecies
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The predictions escalate: a pop quiz question, a fender-bender on Route 9, June's lost ring found exactly where the chat says. The five meet secretly in the library stacks. Emotional beat: giddy thrill curdling into the first real question — who is sending these, and why us?

chapters.title: What Mom Won't Say
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper finds an old photograph in Mom's closet: their grandmother standing on the Founders' Game field beside four strangers — faces that match four of the group chat members' family portraits. Mom deflects when asked. Emotional beat: the discovery that the careful life was built to hide something.

chapters.title: The Founders' Game
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. History of Harrow Creek's centennial tradition: every generation, five families play a ritual game on the last Friday of football season, said to guarantee the town's prosperity. This year the school board is cancelling it — budget cuts, liability. Theo, whose family needs the scholarship tied to the game, panics. Emotional beat: tradition as inheritance and trap.

chapters.title: First Blood Prediction
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The chat sends its first dark message: 'Marcus's brother, Tuesday, the stairs.' Marcus spends Tuesday physically shadowing his little brother, and prevents the fall — but the prediction comes true anyway, just differently. Emotional beat: the horrifying realization that the predictions can't be stopped, only survived.

chapters.title: Five Families, One Bargain
chapters.summary: June's POV. June, the town archivist's granddaughter, digs into the historical society's sealed box: in 1924, five families made a pact after a mine collapse — the Game reenacts it, and someone always pays. Each generation, one player carries the cost. Emotional beat: grief for ancestors who traded safety for survival, and recognition of her own family's silence.

chapters.title: The Cost So Far
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The five map out what each ancestor paid: a business, a marriage, a mind, a son. Vesper realizes their grandmother paid nothing — she left before the last game, which is why the Oyelarans have been outsiders ever since. Emotional beat: Vesper's lifelong 'carefulness' reframed as inherited debt.

chapters.title: Cancelling Is Not Escaping
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The board officially cancels the Game; that night the predictions turn vicious — accidents cluster around the five families like the town itself is collecting. Priya's father loses his job within hours of the vote. Emotional beat: dread — the bargain doesn't need permission to collect.

chapters.title: Rules of Play
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Inside the 1924 rulebook, the five find the terms: if the Game isn't played by season's end, the debt falls due in full, on everyone. But there's a clause — a game can be 'amended by unanimous consent of the blood.' Emotional beat: fragile hope, and the weight of unanimity among five people who barely trust each other.

chapters.title: Fracture
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus wants to play the Game straight and protect his brother; June wants to burn the archive; Theo wants the scholarship; Priya wants out entirely. A fight in the bleachers ends the group chat — someone mutes it. The predictions stop. That's worse. Emotional beat: the terror of silence after noise.

chapters.title: The Empty Chat Speaks
chapters.summary: June's POV. With the chat muted, the messages arrive as physical notes, then as voices — the town itself speaking through small coincidences. June's grandmother finally tells her the truth of 1924: the original five didn't agree to the bargain; the adults sacrificed the youngest among them. Emotional beat: righteous anger becoming resolve.

chapters.title: Vesper's Choice
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Mom collapses from exhaustion; the hospital bills land; Vesper sees the shape of their own future — a lifetime of paying for everyone, carefully, invisibly. For the first time they understand the bargain isn't history, it's a pattern. They unmute the chat. Emotional beat: choosing to stop surviving alone.

chapters.title: Reassembling
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Vesper calls the other four not with a plan but with the truth: what it costs to be the one who holds everything. The confession cracks the group open. They agree to amend the Game together — unanimously — but they don't yet know how. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt on shared damage rather than shared fear.

chapters.title: The Amendment Problem
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The rulebook requires the amendment be spoken on the field during the Game, witnessed by all five bloodlines — but the school board locked the stadium, and the final Friday is six days away. The five plan to reopen the Game publicly, turning tradition into spectacle so the whole town witnesses. Emotional beat: audacity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Rallying the Town
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The five go public: flyers, a petition, stories from families who've quietly paid the price for a century. Half the town calls it superstition; half remembers. The board relents under pressure — one Game, Friday night, broadcast. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, frightening power of being believed.

chapters.title: What the Chat Wants
chapters.summary: June's POV. The chat reveals its sender: not a ghost but the accumulated record itself — the Game's ledger, keeping score, wanting to be settled. It offers each of them a personal deal: your family spared, one name given. Each refuses. Emotional beat: temptation resisted not through heroism but through the refusal to trade anyone.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Quiet chapter: Vesper makes dinner, helps siblings with costumes for the halftime pageant, writes a letter to Mom explaining everything in case it goes wrong. Theo, Priya, Marcus, and June each arrive at the door, one by one, to sit with them. Emotional beat: found family solidifying on the eve of the unknown.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Rotating POV across all five. The Game begins under floodlights before the whole town — a strange, beautiful ritual of relay and reckoning. Midway, the ledger intervenes, demanding its traditional payment, and the crowd watches the five refuse in unison. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into ceremony.

chapters.title: The Amendment
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, climax. On the fifty-yard line, Vesper speaks the amendment: the debt is not erased but redistributed — the whole town becomes signatory, the price shared until it becomes no price at all. The ledger resists; the five hold hands and speak as one bloodline. The chat goes silent mid-sentence. Emotional beat: the moment survival stops meaning sacrifice.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Fallout: the stadium lights flicker and die, the archive box empties, and the town wakes to ordinary weather and no more predictions. Some are grateful; some feel robbed of their story. The five are simply teenagers again, unsure what to do with an unplanned Saturday. Emotional beat: disorientation of freedom.

chapters.title: A New Mixtape
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, resolution. Weeks later: Mom works days now, the siblings argue about breakfast, and Veper burns a mixtape — for themselves, for once. The five meet without agenda. The last scene mirrors the first, but the lunches are packed slower, the care lighter. Emotional beat: belonging without the price tag; identity chosen, not inherited.
